headline: Heard $1,900,000 loan request for 28 affordable units in Centralville; no vote taken; approved $7,500 administrator stipend for 2027.
summary: The board heard a presentation from James Heller on behalf of Residence at Mill Square LLC and The Residence at Bridge Crossing LLC requesting a $1,900,000 loan to create 28 affordable housing units at 27 West Third Street, 18-22 Third Street, and 399-401 Bridge Street. No vote was taken on the loan; the board said it would gather questions and invite Mr. Heller back. The board also approved the July 15th, 2026 meeting minutes and a $7,500 appropriation toward the 2027 AHTF Administrator stipend.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 15th, 2026 AHTF Board meeting, 4-0.
Approved appropriating $7,500.00 toward the 2027 AHTF Administrator stipend, 4-0.

plain_text:
CITY OF LOWELL AFFORDABLE HOUSING TRUST FUND 
MINUTES 
Mayor’s Reception Room, Lowell City Hall  
August 19, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. 
Note: These minutes are not completed verbatim. For further details, contact the Affordable 
Housing Trust Fund or refer to video recordings available online at www.LTC.org.  
Date: August 19, 2026. 
Time: 4:30 pm 
Location: Lowell City Hall (375 Merrimack Street)-2nd Floor (Mayors Reception Room) 
I. Members Present:   Tha Chhan (Ex Officio LHA Director) , Valerie Opara (Vice 
Chairperson), George E. Coulouras (Administrator), Eric Nelson (Chairperson), Cathy Merc 
ado 
Members Absent:  
Others Present: James Heller, Peter Marlowe, David Degan, Jessica Finocchiaro 
The following represents the actions taken by the Affordable Housing Trust Fund at  the 
8/19/2026 meeting.  
II. Meeting Call to Order: 
 Motion made by Eric Nelson to start the meeting  
Seconded by: Tha Chhan 
Vote Approved 4-0 
III. Roll Call Members Present:  Tha Chhan (Ex Officio LHA Director),Cathy Mercado,  
George E. Coulouras (Administrator), Eric Nelson (Chairperson), Valerie Opara. 
IV. Motion made by Chairperson Eric Nelson to approve the minutes of July 15th, 2026, AHTF 
Board meeting. 
Seconded by: Tha Chhan 
Vote Approved 4-0
V. New Business – Presentation from Mr. James Heller on behalf of the  residence at Mill 
Square LLC. and The Residence at Bridge Crossing LLC for a loan funding request of 
$1,900,000.00 (one million nine hundred thousand dollars) for the creation of 28 affordable 
housing units.  
Mr. James Heller was invited to the podium to present his loan request. Mr. Heller thanked 
the AHTF Board for taking the time to meet with his team. He mentioned he is the controller 
for the development team and resides in Lowell.  He introduced the principals of the 
company, who are Peter Marlowe and David Degan. Jim Heller mentioned this presentation 
is given in the name of Residence of West Fourth Street LLC because that is the entity which 
owns the building  at 27 West Third Street. 
Eric Nelson mentioned we will not be taking a vote tonight. We will present the questions in 
the interim or before the next meeting and allow Mr. Heller time to answer at our next meeting 
or report back through staff before next AHTF meeting. 
Mr. Heller started by saying his proposal meets the ARPA program goals for  the creation of 
affordable housing by immediately providing 18 deed restricted affordable housing units. He 
mentioned they also meet the goals of the Lowell Forward Master Plan to  increase 
residential density within transit corridors. He mentioned he meets the goals of FY2026-
FY2030 consolidated plan by addressing the priority need of two-bedroom units. Most of the 
units will be two bedrooms and possibly 6 three bedrooms. He said they are trying to build 
homes for families. 
Technical difficulty  
Administrator requests a ﬁve-minute recess to ﬁx computer issue. 
VI. New  Business Continued- Mr. James Heller returned to the podium to continue his 
presentation. Mr. Heller showed 3 posters of the project showing architectural drawings of 
the buildings from different angles and views. Mr . Heller said what he is asking for is 
$1,900,000.00 @ 2% for 20 years of deed restricted affordability for 28 units. He then broke 
down cost per unit. The 18 units are immediately affordable and then 10 units will come in 
about 15 months although are shovel ready. 
Mr. Heller described the owners and principals as experienced local developers who  keep 
most of the properties they develop and own many in Lowell . Mr. Heller then described the 
rest of his development team. 
Mr. Heller then re -capped his presentation and 18 affordable homes deed restricted at 
closing including 27 West Third Street (12 Deed affordable deed restricted units), 18-22 Third
Street (4 affordable deed restricted units), 399 -401 Bridge Street (2  Affordable deed 
restricted units). 
Mr. Heller then mentioned that his development team goal is to create affordable  family 
housing in Centralville. 
Mr. Heller then described the parking and elevators along with aesthetics of the buildings. 
Mr. Heller mentioned that the owners will manage the buildings themselves and have 
created relationships with The Lowell Housing Authority, CTI and House of Hope. Mr. Heller 
mentioned that this is an investment for the City of Lowell and he is conﬁdent the project is 
ARPA compliant. Mr. Heller explained how they are local and from the neighborhood and the 
goal is to create affordable housing to allow the people of Centralville to stay in the 
neighborhood. Mr. Heller mentioned that the company is local and they manufacture many 
products in Lowell. Mr. Heller stated the beneﬁts of what Lowell receives from granting this 
loan including permit fees, principal and interest payments, secure payback, sustainability, 
tax revenue, local jobs and large scale re-use and homes for families. 
VII. Discussion- Eric Nelson thanked the presenter. Valeria  Opara said Mr Heller mentioned 
he had other sources of funding and what is the total amount of the project? 
Mr. Heller answered $ 4,250,000.00 and the owners will fund any shortage from other 
buildings they own. He said they need the money to meet debt service coverage and increase 
cash ﬂow. Mr. Heller offered a copy of a breakdown of the budget and a copy of his 
presentation and Mr. Coulouras will distribute to the Board. 
Tha Chhan thanked the presenter and appreciates their efforts to create affordable housing. 
Tha asks about the percentage of AMI in the units and do you have a team or process that is 
checking in with the tenants to make sure they qualify? Mr. Heller stated he put together a 
credit selection plan to qualify tenants. 
Tha Chhan ask for more detail about the ﬁnancing and fair Housing plan put together on the 
project . Mr. Heller said he would provide. 
Jessica Finocchiaro spoke to the language around the compliance piece and that  if there is 
an agreement approved that we have already reached out to law for  the need to expedite  
compliance. 
Cathy Mercado thanked the presenter and appreciated the developers work. She mentioned 
she had many questions and will save them to present at next meeting and is worried about 
how they will stay affordable for the residents they are targeting. She then thanked the 
presenter.
Eric Nelson stated he had many questions and will forward to all and present to the board. 
He wanted to ensure from the City of Lowell that this is ARPA compliant. 
Jessica Finocchiaro stated the City of Lowell Executive Staff has conﬁrmed that this project 
is ARPA eligible and the Executive Staff has reviewed the application for eligibility. She 
mentioned that if there is a sale then the deed restriction survives but the loan must be paid 
back. 
Eric Nelson asks  if the 18 Units are currently affordable? Jim Heller said no they will be 
created to be affordable with these funds. Eric Nelson suggested that our 1.9 million allows 
the development team to recapitalize their existing loans to give the developer better 
qualiﬁcations to get a new loan.  
Eric Nelson questioned the concurrence from Mass Historical Commission ? Mr. Heller 
stated that they meet all Mass Historical Commission guidelines. 
Eric Nelson mentioned in closing that he appreciates the 2 - and 3 -bedroom units being 
offered .  
VIII. Continued Business – Eric Nelson ask if the Executive Staff has other projects in the 
pipeline which they are working on and need to be cogni zant of for  the utilization of our 
funds? 
IX. Discussion Jessica Finocchiaro mentioned yes there are other request in the pipeline 
although this project ﬁt the ARPA compliance and vetting process best and this project is a 
low price per unit cost for affordability. 
The AHTF Board thanked Mr. Heller and asked for time to formulate questions regarding the 
presentation and will invite him back to answer the board’s questions. 
X. Continued Business - Appropriation of $7500.00 toward the 2027 AHTF Administrator 
stipend. 
XI. Discussion-   
Motion made by Eric Nelson  to appropriate $7500.00 toward the 2027 AHTF Administrator 
stipend 
Seconded by Tha Chhan  
Vote approved 4-0 
XII Continued Business- The loan servicer for the  AHTF loans and replied and they will begin 
possible servicing the AHTF loans for second quarter of 2027 and for now the Administrator 
is collecting the payments and turning them into the Treasurer.
XIII. Next Meeting scheduled for August 19, 2026 @ 4:30 in The Mayors Reception Room 
XIV. Motion to adjourn – Made by Eric Nelson (chairperson) 
Seconded by Tha Chhan 
Vote Approved 4-0 
Meeting Adjourned
